_comment: The POOL, not a payload: what fetch/news.py reads before news/rule.yaml has been applied to it. Every entry is a dated statement read off a public release record in this estate's own organisations, which is why each one carries a URL anybody can open. The last entry is here to be REFUSED: it has no provenance URL, so the rule does not admit it, which is the mechanism that keeps an invented headline -- a SCENARIO -- out of a feed of observations. Upgrade path: swap lib.read_upstream() for a GET of a real news or press-release endpoint; the admission rule below it does not change.
source: Publisher release records in the policy-as-versioned organisations

events.statement: ico published the signed tag v1.0.0 of its penalty schema.
platform published the signed tag policy/v3.0.0, described by its own release commit as a major repair release.
nist published the signed tag v1.1.0 of its controls catalogue.
platform published the signed tag v1.1.1 of its implementations package, carrying release-gate evidence for policy/v3.0.0.
Somebody said a thing, and no URL was recorded for where it was read.
